newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran firm gains edge in Soroush bid - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran firm gains edge in Soroush bid - MEES.

text.p: State-owned Iranian Offshore Engineering Construction Company (IOEC) is leading the bidding to develop Iran's offshore Soroush oilfield, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
"IOEC appears to be gaining the edge in the bidding for Soroush," the Cyprus-based weekly said.
Soroush is one of the five offshore oil and gas field development projects offered by National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) under its "buy-back" formula in an attempt to boost offshore capacity.
IOEC, headed by Mehdi Hashimi Rafsanjani, son of the Iranian President, is 51 percent NIOC-owned with the remaining 49 percent held by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

Soroush project, which had also attracted the interest of foreign firm, envisages redeveloping the field -- seriously damaged during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war -- to a capacity of 90,000 barrels per day (bpd) at a cost of around $200 million.
Iranian officials have said that an award on Soroush and the 40,000 bpd capacity Balal field is expected by the end of March and that local firms will take a major slice of work.
IOEC has been in the bidding process since last year.
A successful foreign bidder could fall foul of the U.S. Iran-Libya Sanctions Act which aims to deter foreign investment in Iranian energy.

France's Total SA TOTF.PA) and Malaysia's state-owned Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) are to date the only direct foreign presence in offshore work under a contract to develop the Sirri E and A oil and gas fields.
IOEC is already carrying out offshore work that was originally set aside to be carried out by foreign firms.

The company's position in the bidding for Soroush had been strengthened by securing two loan packages totalling $160 million from the commodity trade finance group at Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank WDLGg.D MEES reported.
"The first tranche of the loan, for $90 million, has been secured and documentation is expected to be ready for signature by the end of March," MEES said.
"The second facility, totaling $70 million, is not scheduled to be disbursed for another 12 to 18 months pending finalisation of package details," it reported.
Financing facilities are earmarked specifically for Soroush and do not involve any other development project.
Repayment would be guaranteed by NIOC through the proceeds of crude oil sold under existing NIOC supply contracts and not from production from Soroush itself.
NIOC is responsible for Iran's 2.5 million bpd of crude exports, the world's third major source of oil.

"It is further understood that repayment of the loan is to begin two and a half years after commencement of construction work on the Soroush project, regardless as to whether or not the development work is completed," MEES said.
West Deutsche Landes Bank is already financing IOEC's work at the offshore Abuzar development.
